principles: Keep source extraction, normalization, calculation, inference, manual editing and publication provenance separate.
Never silently replace a source value with a calculated, inferred or normalized value.
Treat AI output as a review proposal; deterministic validation and human acceptance govern publication.
Apply rules generally to all wells, reports, scans, tables, file types and survey layouts.
Keep named wells and page ranges only in regression fixtures, never in general discovery assumptions.

requirements: Inspect the complete source, including page images, appendices, landscape pages, rotated pages and pages with weak or absent parsed text.
Do not reject a source merely because searchable text does not expose the survey.
Use table geometry and repeated column positions when OCR headers are weak.
Preserve PDF page number and printed or table page number separately.
Resolve the exact well, wellbore and sidetrack before creating primary candidates.
Do not assign parent-well survey data to a sidetrack, or sidetrack data to the parent, without explicit evidence.
Use well name, UWI, report title, repeated page headers and section context as evidence.
Only confirmed_selected_well is automatically primary-candidate eligible.
Assemble related cover, metadata, station, comment and marker pages only when the relationship is defensible.
Use matching well identity, run title, units, coordinate convention, continuous MD range, repeated headers, page numbering or explicit continuation language.
Do not combine pages merely because they occur near each other.
Separate different survey dates, tools, contractors, runs, hole sections, sidetracks, planned surveys and actual surveys.

workflow: retain page and cell image coordinates

requirements: Preserve original direction notation before producing signed normalized values.
Do not call local offsets global northings or eastings unless explicitly defined.
Preserve source units and normalized units separately.
Do not treat deg/30m and deg/100ft as numerically equivalent.
Keep missing source cells null; calculated completion remains separately identified.

qaqc_rules.rule: Every accepted primary station requires numeric MD, inclination and azimuth.
Accepted primary MD must be strictly increasing.
Duplicate MD with different INC/AZI requires review and must not be silently discarded.
Flag a large unexplained MD gap relative to local station spacing.
Inclination must be between 0 and 180 degrees.
Normalized azimuth must be between 0 and less than 360 degrees.
Flag abrupt azimuth reversals, with reduced significance at near-zero inclination.
Flag source TVD greater than MD when referenced in the same unit and datum.
Compare source TVD with independent calculation without replacing the source value.
Direction letters and normalized coordinate signs must agree.
Flag abrupt lateral jumps inconsistent with course length, inclination and azimuth.
Negative DLS is invalid; unusually high DLS uses configurable warning thresholds rather than universal rejection.
Mixed unresolved depth units block publication.
Mixed unresolved dogleg denominators block reliable DLS comparison.
Missing or conflicting MD datum, TVD datum, coordinate origin or azimuth reference requires review.
Run duplicate, continuity, unit and clipped-digit checks at every source-page boundary.
Flag uncertain decimal points, direction letters and ambiguous critical characters.
Do not merge different wells, sidetracks, planned and actual surveys, or conflicting runs.
Extrapolated stations must remain explicitly marked and not counted as measured.
Casing positions are related markers and do not automatically enter the primary station sequence.
Publication requires confirmed applicability, resolved units, at least two accepted stations and no unresolved failures.

comparison_tolerances.note: These are configurable QAQC review thresholds, not automatic rejection thresholds.

requirements: Only accepted or edited rows are publishable.
At least two accepted stations are required.
Accepted MD must be strictly increasing.
Depth and angle units must be resolved.
Well applicability must be confirmed.
Extrapolated rows must remain explicit.
Source and calculated values must both remain available.
WBV must consume the published trajectory independently of WDV.
